misconceptions.description: Assuming rigid-body equilibrium only requires force balance
misconceptions.trigger: learner sets sum Fx and sum Fy to zero but omits the moment equation
misconceptions.feedback: A rigid body can rotate even when the net force is zero. In 2D statics, you need sum Fx = 0, sum Fy = 0, and sum M = 0.

misconceptions.description: Forgetting that a fixed support resists rotation
misconceptions.trigger: learner models a cantilever support with force reactions only
misconceptions.feedback: A fixed support in 2D provides two force components and a reaction moment. Omitting the reaction moment makes the support model incomplete.

misconceptions.description: Using a nonperpendicular distance in the moment term
misconceptions.trigger: learner multiplies force by an arbitrary slanted distance
misconceptions.feedback: Moments use the perpendicular distance from the reference point to the line of action of the force, not just any measured length.
